title: Traffic Policy Playbook: Tactical Scenario Simulator & Emergency Swap Panel
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype an interactive 'Traffic Policy Playbook' that lets SREs and product engineers compose, simulate, and execute tactical rollout scenarios (gradual canaries, hypothesis-driven A/B splits, emergency swap to fallback models). The experience should: expose safety gates, show expected KPI impact, permit fast emergency swaps with one-click rollback, and produce a human-readable runbook summary for postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive simulator accepts policy inputs (percentage ramps, quiesce windows, experiment split criteria) and renders expected latency/cost/KPI curves
Emergency Swap panel allows immediate model swap or traffic diversion to a fallback and shows estimated cost/latency delta before confirmation
Runbook export generated automatically with timeline, alerts triggered, and rollback steps
Design receives engineering feasibility sign-off and a small prototype is validated in user-research with at least 6 platform engineers/product owners
All primary screens have annotated accessibility considerations and clear error states

Follow-ups: 1) Finalize copy for emergency confirmations; 2) Add telemetry events list for engineers to validate observability; 3) Coordinate with PM to draft comms for beta users.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Estimating KPI deltas from sampled traffic can be misleading for small canaries — mitigated with explicit confidence intervals and conservative default ramps
Exposing too many knobs will confuse users; we prioritize presets and guided flows over full-surface policy editing in v1
One-click emergency swap risks accidental activation; require two-step confirmation and optional 'safety pin' that requires SRE role to unlock
user_research_summary: 6 sessions with platform engineers and product owners
Key finding: timeline + projected KPI curves give confidence faster than raw table metrics
Users want an easily exportable runbook snippet to paste into incident channels
Preset templates (Canary Ramp, A/B Hypothesis Test, Dark Launch) were used in 85% of test runs
